source: https://www.cordsurfboards.com/surfboards (Wix model lineup — excludes fins, apparel, merch, and other-shaper stock boards)

brands.name: Cord Surfboards
brands.short_description: Family-shaped custom surfboards founded in Caloundra, Australia in 1965 by David Lascelles and now built to order by head shaper Markie Lascelles in St Agnes, Cornwall.

models.name: Flying Vee
models.description: Markie Lascelles' original swallow-tail twin fish. A wider plan shape and flatter rocker make it a strong paddler with acceleration and drive through the wide swallow tail. Deep spiral vee between the twin boxes gives rail-to-rail response in critical sections and on flatter faces — a small-wave summer cruiser that still flies in waves up to 6ft.

models.name: Humbucker
models.description: A snub-nosed, high-volume twin-fin swallow named after the dual-coil guitar pickup for extra volume and bite. A beaked nose keeps foam under the chest, low rocker and a wider outline add paddle power, and a short split channel between the boxes lifts the tail through turns. Looks like a small-wave board but has become Markie's go-to in 6ft-plus barrels.

models.name: Kingswood
models.description: Cord's old-faithful noserider, born from the long right-hand points of Noosa. Goes in anything above a ripple and is really fun in waves up to 3ft: take off, pick your line, walk to the nose and stay there.

models.name: Projector
models.description: Cord's performance all-rounder mid-length. Testers felt it projected around sections. Volume for small or bigger waves, a pulled-in nose to duck dive, a drawn-out rail line and a relatively flat bottom contour for a fast, drivey 2+1.

models.name: Sawn-Off
models.description: A longboard with a section cut out of the middle. Offers the longboard vibe but is easier to handle, turns more easily, and still noserides in the pocket thanks to a deep nose concave. Super fun in waves up to 4ft.

models.name: Step-Ark
models.description: Step-up version of the channel-bottom twin-fin pintail Ark, made for bigger, hollower waves. Designed with Noah Lane, developed for Irish slabs, and proven up to 12ft.

models.name: Sunseeker
models.description: Cord's go-to mid-length funboard, made for small summer days and tested in waves up to 6ft. Lots of volume and flat rocker for paddling, spiral vee for a smooth rail-to-rail feel, and a fuller outline with a slightly drawn-in nose and rounded pin tail.

models.name: Swordfish
models.description: Cord's high-performance shortboard, developed with Noah Lane for a Maldives trip. A wider nose and forward wide point help paddle entry, while the drawn-in back half, square-cut swallow tail and fluted tail channels are built for tight turns, airs and barrels in waves up to 6ft.

models.name: The Ark
models.description: Cord's best-seller: a four-channel twin-fin pintail designed with Australian charger Noah Lane. Extra volume under the chest helps wave-catching, and the channel-bottom twin setup is made for speed and turning in 3–6ft waves.

models.name: The Classic
models.description: Drawn from the original 1965 Cord factory template in Caloundra. Wide point set back, rolled belly vee toward the fin, old-style 50/50 rails, a narrower nose and a single nose concave for noseriding in the pocket in clean waves up to 4ft.

models.name: The Otter
models.description: Swallow-tail sibling of the Ark. Head shaper Markie Lascelles pulled in the nose and tail of the Ark template for a more performance outline, kept a single concave running into four tail channels, and released it through a baby swallow. An all-round board from regular to well-overhead hollow waves.

models.name: The Sailfish
models.description: A long fish designed for maximum speed and flow down the line, with the ability to hold a rail and turn on a dime.
